name: Boneyard — Vintage Chrome & Aug Resale Net
description: Boneyard is GLMZ's dominant secondary market for used, vintage, and salvaged augmentation hardware — a sprawling digital bazaar where chrome techs, the Gray Zone scavengers, aug collectors, and body modification enthusiasts trade everything from decommissioned military-grade limbs to artisan-crafted cosmetic implants from defunct boutique labs. Founded in 2195 by Cassiel Nduka-Petrov, a former the Gray Zone chrome tech who started the platform after watching clients die from counterfeit aug installations when they couldn't afford new, Boneyard operates on a strict community verification system where experienced techs certify hardware condition before listing. The platform's 'ghost section' — accessible via Underworld routing — lists aug hardware with no certification and no questions asked.
cultural_impact: Boneyard has democratized access to functional augmentation hardware for the Gray Zone and working-class residents who cannot afford new installations, creating a thriving secondary aug economy that corponation medical device manufacturers actively lobby against. The platform's certification community has become an informal credentialing system for chrome techs — a 'Boneyard-certified' technician carries genuine street credibility that rivals official corponation licensing in Tier 1-2 communities.
locations: Boneyard Hub, Pilsen Hardware Row, Tier 2
The Ossuary Alley, the Gray Zone district 4 (physical inspection meet point)
Ghost Section mirror, Underworld node cluster
story_hooks: A batch of decommissioned military-grade chrome surfaces on Boneyard's ghost section — hardware that was officially destroyed in a corponation audit — and every buyer who installs it starts receiving encrypted signals they can't identify or block.

Cassiel Nduka-Petrov is pressured by a medical device corponation to implement mandatory serial number reporting on all listings, which would expose every the Gray Zone buyer to corporate surveillance — and refuses, triggering a legal assault designed to bankrupt the platform.

The Verification Guild splits over whether to certify a new category of aug: harvested synthetic components — functional hardware removed from decommissioned synthetic beings — raising profound ethical questions about synthetic personhood and whether their bodies can be sold as parts.
user_base: Approximately 3.7 million registered users; predominantly Tier 1-2 chrome techs, aug enthusiasts, the Gray Zone residents seeking affordable hardware, and Tier 3 vintage collectors seeking discontinued aesthetic pieces
monetization: Listing fees (flat Φ12 per standard listing, Φ0 for the Gray Zone-flagged users under income threshold); optional Verification Guild certification fees (paid to the Guild, not the platform); ghost section access subscription (Φ180/month, Underworld routing included); dispute resolution escrow services
notable_feature: The Verification Guild's certification system is entirely community-run and cannot be purchased or expedited — a piece of hardware can sit in verification queue for weeks while Guild members physically inspect it, a deliberately slow process that has made Boneyard certifications genuinely trustworthy in a market full of counterfeits
